problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: Find an approximate zero of F+A, where F:E→E is L-Lipschitz and A:E⇉E is monotone with an everywhere-defined resolvent for each positive stepsize.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: The problem is a cohypomonotone operator inclusion. For u∈(F+A)(x) and v∈(F+A)(y), ⟨u−v,x−y⟩ ≥ −ρ‖u−v‖² throughout the range 0≤ρL<1.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: A query (γ,z) with γ>0 returns the exact resolvent y=(I+γA)⁻¹z, giving the graph witness (z−y)/γ∈A(y). Stochastic evaluations and resolvent evaluations each consume one call from the same fixed budget.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: A query at x returns one vector g(x,ξ) from an unbiased stochastic operator oracle for F. Each call uses a fresh seed. The query interface gives the algorithm neither the seed nor a way to reuse it at another point.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: The seeds are independent with common law p. At every x, Eₚ[g(x,ξ)]=F(x) and Eₚ‖g(x,ξ)−F(x)‖²≤σ². The Lipschitz bound applies to the mean operator F.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The spaces, starting point x₀ and parameters L>0, 0≤ρ<1/L, R≥0, σ≥0 and ε>0 are public. The operators F and A are hidden. Some solution x⋆ satisfies −F(x⋆)∈A(x⋆) and ‖x₀−x⋆‖≤R.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The measurable output is a pair (x,a). Its second component must satisfy a∈A(x) for every outcome.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The residual norm ‖F(x)+a‖ of the returned pair must be integrable and satisfy E‖F(x)+a‖≤ε. The expectation uses the joint law of the algorithm and oracle seeds.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines negative comonotonicity of the sum up to ρL<1 with noisy access to F and exact resolvent access to A. Accuracy is measured using the graph element that the algorithm actually returns.

descriptionHtml:
Full-Range Cohypomonotone Inclusions

We seek a zero of F+A on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The map F:E→E is L-Lipschitz with L>0, the set-valued operator A:E⇉E is monotone, and F+A is ρ-cohypomonotone with 0≤ρ<1/L. A given point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a solution. The oracle provides unbiased estimates of F with bounded variance using independent, identically distributed samples, or exact resolvent values of A at positive step sizes. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable pair (x¯,a¯) with a¯∈A(x¯) for every realization and E∥F(x¯)+a¯∥≤ε, averaging over oracle and algorithm randomness.

In terms of a point x⋆ and a vector a⋆, the inclusion is to find x⋆∈E,a⋆∈A(x⋆),F(x⋆)+a⋆=0. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0, and the parameters L,ρ,R,σ,ε, where σ≥0 bounds the root mean squared oracle error.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Operator inequalities). For all x,y∈E, ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥. For every a∈A(x) and b∈A(y), write u=F(x)+a and v=F(y)+b. Monotonicity of A and cohypomonotonicity of F+A mean that ⟨a−b,x−y⟩≥0,⟨u−v,x−y⟩≥−ρ∥u−v∥2.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance). There exists a solution x⋆ of the inclusion such that ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic evaluations and resolvent access). At call k, a query x∈E returns g(x,ξk), where g:E×Ω→E is jointly measurable. The samples (ξk)k≥0 are independent random variables with common law ν on Ω, and the sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. For each x∈E and ξ∼ν, the vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, the squared error ∥g(x,ξ)−F(x)∥2 is integrable, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=F(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−F(x)∥2]≤σ2. Alternatively, a query (γ,z)∈R×E returns Jγ(z)∈E. For every γ>0 and z∈E, this reply satisfies the resolvent identity z−Jγ(z)γ∈A(Jγ(z)). Both query types draw on the same call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output (x¯,a¯)∈E×E must be measurable and satisfy a¯∈A(x¯) for every realization. Under the joint law P of the samples and the algorithm’s randomness, the residual norm must be integrable and satisfy EP[∥F(x¯)+a¯∥]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
In a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, F is L-Lipschitz (L>0), G is maximal monotone, and F+G is ρ-cohypomonotone with 0≤ρL<1. Some zero x⋆ of F+G satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Each call gives an exact resolvent of G or a jointly measurable, unbiased sample of F with variance at most σ2 using IID randomness. The target is a measurable pair (x,u) with u∈G(x) for every seed and E∥F(x)+u∥≤ε, ε>0.

Sufficient oracle budgets for full-range stochastic cohypomonotone inclusions.

(1) FullRangeCohypomonotoneMlmc (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+a/τ+bτ2ℓ7(1+a+bτ)) deterministic calls
(2) Inexact Halpern (Alacaoglu et al. 2026, Cor. 4.1) O(K4ℓ2(K)/τ2) for the last-iterate resolvent residual ∥z−Jη(F+G)z∥/η in root mean square. (1): For fixed L,R,ρ and σ>0, the cost drops from fourth to second order in 1/ε, up to logarithms as ε↓0, with an explicit graph certificate throughout ρL<1. (1) bounds the mean norm. (2) controls the second moment of its resolvent residual for maximally ρ-cohypomonotone F+G.
(3) RAIN++ (Chen and Luo 2025, Thm. 5.4 and Prop. 5.3) O~(1+a+b) expected samples, including conversion from saddle-envelope to original gradient accuracy. (1) extends (3) from unconstrained saddle-gradient operators (G=0, ρL≤1/2) to composite inclusions with ρL<1. On the overlap, polynomial rates match and (1) fixes the budget per seed.
(4) Regularized prox-extragradient (LongTails 2026b) O(1+a+bδ8ℓ4(1+aδ)) (1) extends ρL<1/2 to ρL<1. As ρL↑1/2, its condition factors stay bounded while (4) grows at least as δ−8. (1) has a seventh-power logarithm involving noise. (4) has a fourth-power logarithm independent of noise.
(5) Multistep anchored method (LongTails 2026a) O(1+⌈a/τ⌉ℓ(1/τ)/τ) exact calls. (1) allows finite-variance samples where (5) requires exact F. With exact F and a≥1, (1) pays a/τ3 times a seventh-power logarithm. (5) pays aℓ(1/τ)/τ2.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticCohypomonotoneInclusion

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.FullRangeCohypomonotoneInclusion

open OracleTemplate
open LongTails.Setups.StochasticCohypomonotoneInclusion (Params reply)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := (p.E → p.E) × (p.E → Set p.E)
  Query p := p.E ⊕ (ℝ × p.E)
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E × p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.ρ ∧ q.ρ * q.L < 1 ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I O :=
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticCohypomonotoneInclusion.spec.admissible q I O
  successful q I output P :=
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticCohypomonotoneInclusion.spec.successful q I output P

end LongTails.Setups.FullRangeCohypomonotoneInclusion
